newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - NYH gasoline still firm with MTBE.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - NYH gasoline still firm with MTBE.

text.p: Gasoline in New York Harbor continued to be firm on the back of MTBE, while gasoline in Houston firmed amid a lack of liquidity, which softened differentials in Houston, traders said.
NYMEX gasoline was the beneficiary of a healthy round of bull spread trading apparently led by independent refiner Tosco, or at least its proxies on the NYMEX floor.
August gasoline settled a sharp 1.09 cents higher at 62.21 cents a gallon, while August heat rose just 0.11 cent settling at 53.39 cents a gallon.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Reformulated and high octane gasoline grades remained at firmer levels amid strong prices of the blending component MTBE as well as fewer cargoes that are tightening supplies.

"Demand (for gasoline) has been exceptional. As long as MTBE continues strong, the A2 (reformulated) and D2 (high octane) grades will be too. On the other hand, there is plenty of conventional gasoline," said a New York Harbor trader.
Reformulated A2 grade was done at 2.35 and 2.25 cents over the NYMEX. Conventional unleaded was bid at 4.50 cents under NYMEX versus 4.25 cents this morning.
A trader said high octane D2 grade was done at 12.00 cents over NYMEX after being offered at 11.75 cents Wednesday. Imports have been decreasing, adding to supply concerns.
"While the arb from Europe is not shut it is not as open as it once was, so fewer imports are coming," said a dealer.
U.S. GULF
Gasoline differentials in Houston staged a rally late Thursday afternoon after starting the day humming quietly along amid a lack of liquidity.

That lack of liquidity never quite went away, in part due to an industry function BP was staging Thursday in Cleveland and some traders said perhaps prices were being readily manipulated with so many players missing.

Newly-prompt back 21st cycle "M1" regular conventional southern-grade unleaded was heard done at levels as firm as 1.25 cents under August NYMEX after starting the day at about 2.25 cents under the print.
On the distillate side, differentials were a bit firmer and activity was moderately active.
Prompt 86-grade heating oil was about a quarter cent firmer than on Wednesday pegged at between 2.25 and 2.00 cents under the print.
Prompt low sulphur 74-grade was heard done at 1.20 and 1.25 cents under the August print, and prompt 54-grade airline-quality 54-grade jet fuel was done at 0.45 cent over.
MIDCONTINENT
Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials plunged about a cent in quiet trade on Thursday, largely because of a lack of buyers and the one penny rise of NYMEX August gasoline.
"The absolute values are still the same. It's just basis points coming in line with NYMEX," said a trader.

Group Three unleaded had been up about a half cent since Monday, rising on hype over a small fire at National Cooperative Refinery Association's McPherson, Kansas, plant. Few deals, however, were done at the higher levels.
Thursday afternoon, Group unleaded differentials were pegged 0.25 cent under the print, with Chicago market material holding steady at 0.75/1.00 over the screen.
--New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
